beats.narration_text: Shalom — this is Liam, in for Divyank. Ask which API technology is 'better' — FastAPI or gRPC — and you're already asking the wrong question. Real systems run both, on purpose, for completely different reasons. Let's take apart what each one actually is, and why neither one replaces the other.

send arms, runningText plays
RESULT lines land in sequence

props.command: Compare FastAPI and gRPC properly: architecture, why a real system would run both, their actual use cases, and the tradeoffs nobody mentions.
output: running both is division of labor, not redundancy
the format that's easy to read is expensive to move at scale

beats.act: Act I — Two Answers to One Question
beats.narration_text: R-P-C means remote procedure call — making a function run on another machine feel like calling it locally. Both FastAPI and gRPC solve that exact same old problem. They just answer it completely differently.

shot.prompt: real archival telephone-switchboard photo -- illustrative of a remote procedure call, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A1-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push across the switchboard
serif label lands: 'the same old problem'

beats.act: Act I — Two Answers to One Question
beats.narration_text: Pick HTTP 1.1 with JSON, or HTTP 2 with protobuf. One request per connection versus many multiplexed streams on a single connection. Readable text versus a compact binary wire format compiled straight from a schema.

show.event: question card: 'HTTP/1.1 + JSON, or HTTP/2 + protobuf?'
two outcomes: readable / compact

branches.label: HTTP/1.1 + JSON
branches.detail: readable text, one request at a time

beats.act: Act II — Why You'd Run Both
beats.narration_text: Somebody has to stand between a browser that only speaks JSON and a fleet of internal services that only speak protobuf. That's a real job, with a real name — the gateway.

shot.prompt: real archival photo of translators at work -- illustrative of a gateway translating between two protocols, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A2-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push across the booth
serif label lands: 'a real job — the gateway'

beats.act: Act II — Why You'd Run Both
beats.narration_text: One incoming request, two different lives. To the browser: a readable JSON response, debuggable in dev tools. Behind the gateway: the same data, as a compact protobuf call, multiplexed over one persistent connection to a dozen internal services.

show.event: two tracks diverge: the browser-facing response, the internal gRPC call

data.splitLabel: to the browser / behind the gateway

tracks.label: To the browser
tracks.outcome: readable JSON, debuggable in dev tools

tracks.label: Behind the gateway
tracks.outcome: compact protobuf, multiplexed to internal services

beats.act: Act II — Why You'd Run Both
beats.narration_text: Build one API that tries to serve browsers and internal services equally, or split the two. One API for both means every internal call pays the tax of browser-friendly JSON. Splitting them means each side gets the format it actually needs.

show.event: question card: 'one API for both, or split them?'
two outcomes: one API / split

data.question: One API for both, or split them?

branches.label: One API for both
branches.detail: every internal call pays JSON's tax

branches.label: Split them
branches.detail: each side gets its own format
branches.fix: two things to run instead of one

beats.act: Act III — What Each One Is Actually For
beats.narration_text: A battery-powered device, reporting sensor readings over a constrained connection, cannot afford to repeat a JSON object's field names on every single message. Every byte is a cost it actually pays.

shot.prompt: real archival microcontroller macro photo -- illustrative of a constrained IoT device, not a claim about any specific product. Already sourced, see media/A3-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push into the board
serif label lands: 'every byte is a cost it pays'

beats.act: Act IV — The Tradeoffs Nobody Mentions
beats.narration_text: Debug a failing FastAPI call: open dev tools, read the JSON, done. Debug a failing gRPC call: decode a binary payload against a dot-proto schema, or reach for a specialized tool built for exactly that job.

show.event: question card: 'debugging a failing call — how hard?'
two outcomes: FastAPI / gRPC

data.question: Debugging a failing call — how hard?

branches.label: FastAPI
branches.detail: open dev tools, read the JSON

resolver.label: Readability has a cost either way
resolver.detail: it's just paid by a different side

beats.act: Act IV — The Tradeoffs Nobody Mentions
beats.narration_text: The same architectural choice, two outcomes. Pick FastAPI everywhere: every internal call pays JSON's parsing and bandwidth cost, for debuggability it never actually needed. Pick gRPC everywhere: every public client needs a proxy layer just to ask a question.

show.event: two tracks diverge: FastAPI-everywhere, gRPC-everywhere

tracks.label: FastAPI everywhere
tracks.outcome: internal calls pay JSON's cost, for nothing

tracks.label: gRPC everywhere
tracks.outcome: every public client needs a proxy

beats.narration_text: Your turn — here's the prompt, read it with me. 'Design the API layer for one real system I'm building: name which parts face a browser or third party, which parts are internal service-to-service calls, whether any of them actually need streaming, and whether I need one gateway or two separate APIs — and the one tradeoff I'd be accepting either way.' Run it. Liam, in for Divyank.
